bugs.error_message: /api/v0/backends not available HTTP 404 (headless server web UI)
bugs.root_cause: Settings CRUD endpoints (backends + caps/manifests) only existed in the desktop crate (crates/desktop/src/main.rs). The headless n3ur0n serve binary served the bundled web UI but didn't mount those routes, so the Settings tab showed HTTP 404 in browser mode.
bugs.fix: Extracted settings handlers into crates/server/src/settings.rs (pub fn router). cli::serve now merges it into the axum app. Desktop crate dropped its local copy and uses n3ur0n_server::settings::router. Both paths now expose identical Settings APIs.

bugs.error_message: planner dispatch HTTP 500: backend transport: error sending request for url (http://192.168.4.101:11434/v1/chat/completions)
bugs.root_cause: Stale per-node volume fixture pointed planner backend at LAN box 192.168.4.101; OrbStack container bridge cannot route to LAN IPs (host can, containers cannot). Compile LLM call failed -> 500. Unrelated to P2.
bugs.fix: Repointed gpt-oss-20b.toml base_url to http://host.docker.internal:11434 + default_model llama3.1:8b (reachable from containers via host-gateway), restarted node-a. Smoke PASSED.

bugs.error_message: test grammar_escapes_quotes_in_names FAILED - GBNF terminal emitted `"we"ird"`, inner quote unescaped
bugs.root_cause: gbnf_json_string escaped only ONE layer. Two stack: the model emits JSON (a `"` in a name arrives as `\"`), and GBNF terminals are themselves double-quoted, so that backslash AND that quote each need a further GBNF escape. Single-layer escaping lets a quote close the terminal early and corrupts every rule after it.
bugs.fix: Serialise with serde_json::to_string first (JSON layer), then escape backslashes then quotes for the GBNF layer. A name containing `"` now renders as `\\\"` in the grammar.

bugs.error_message: duplicate values in JSON-schema `enum` for peer/capability (found by review, not by a failing test)
bugs.root_cause: Used Vec::dedup() on the peer list. Vec::dedup only removes CONSECUTIVE duplicates. The list is deduped by (peer,capability) PAIR, so a peer exposing several caps repeats non-consecutively and survived.
bugs.fix: Added unique_in_order(): HashSet-based dedup preserving first-seen order, applied to both peer and capability enums. Added test json_schema_enums_have_no_duplicates with a peer exposing 2 caps and a cap name shared by 2 peers.

bugs.error_message: Capability output blobs never appear in the Files panel (Inbound category always empty)
bugs.root_cause: record_inbound_output indexed downloaded output blobs with local_user_id=None and client_id=None, while storage::blobs::list_user_visible selects on `local_user_id = ?1 OR client_id = ?2`. Two NULLs match neither branch, so every user_visible output row was unreachable: stored, GC-counted, invisible. No owner context was threaded from the planner down to the blob index.
bugs.fix: Added BlobOwner {client_id, conversation_id}, built from ConversationState in plan_exec.rs and threaded through execute_plan_streaming -> fetch_output_blobs -> record_inbound_output. Also sets capability and a derived provisional path. Regression test crates/server/tests/blob_outputs.rs, verified to fail against the old code.

bugs.error_message: Planner fabricates a completed action when the user message contains no request ("Je vous ai ouvert le fichier ... sur votre appareil")
bugs.root_cause: A message made only of @ mentions scopes the catalogue but asks nothing. The reflect system prompt opens with 'The user asked a question and a plan was executed; you now have the blackboard', which presupposes both. With an empty plan and an empty blackboard the model filled the blank from the conversation tail and reported having opened a file attached in an earlier turn. The existing honesty rule only covered 'the user asked for a side effect and no tool did it' — not 'the user asked for nothing and you invented both request and action'.
bugs.fix: mention::is_scope_only/strip_mentions detect a mention-only message; reflect_only then injects a system line saying there is no request, do not guess, do not claim anything was done. Reflect prompt also gained a general rule: the blackboard is the complete record, the composer performs no action itself and must never claim one. Verified against qwen2.5:7b on a live node: the same message now answers 'Je n'ai pas de contexte sur cette mention. Pouvez-vous me dire ce que vous souhaitez faire ?'

bugs.error_message: Reflect retypes tool outputs instead of quoting them: reply showed 'Z29601:06:08-12-09-2026' where reverse had returned 'Z706178087.92:60:81T21-90-6202'
bugs.root_cause: blackboard_summary renders '- peer::capability -> value' with no step id, so the composer has no handle for a value and can only retype it. A 7B asked to state a reversed string re-derives the reversal in its head and gets it wrong; a short number beside it (char count) is copied correctly, which is why only long opaque strings drift. Observed with 9-digit nanosecond timestamps on Linux (30 chars); not reproduced on macOS where timestamps are 27 chars.
bugs.fix: referenceable_values() lists '${step.field} = value' tokens in the reflect prompt, the prompt instructs the composer to write the reference rather than the value, and resolve_value substitutes them in the returned reply. Unresolvable references degrade to visible text. Mechanism unit-tested; the end-to-end symptom was not reproducible locally.

bugs.error_message: A ToolCall could be persisted without its ToolResult: persist_tool_pair_at wrote the pair in two separate transactions
bugs.root_cause: persist_tool_pair_at looped over (call, result) calling conversations::append_turn once each, and append_turn opens its own transaction. If the second insert failed — a seq collision, a lock, a disk error — the call stayed committed. The reloaded conversation then showed an invocation that never returned, and the planner's context gained a question with no answer. The executor's hook only logs the error, so execution continued.
bugs.fix: Added conversations::append_turns writing every turn in one transaction; append_turn is now a one-element wrapper. persist_tool_pair_at builds both records then writes them together. Regression test squats the result's seq to force the second insert to fail and asserts nothing is left behind — verified to fail against the old code (3 turns instead of 2).

bugs.error_message: OPEN — continuation rounds still invisible in the cluster UI (no second chip group, no round separator)
bugs.root_cause: UNVERIFIED. Leading hypothesis: the Docker cluster image is a release build, so the UI is embedded by rust-embed AND the PlanReady.round field comes from the node binary — neither the JS nor the Rust change is live until the image is rebuilt. Check `docker compose -f docker/compose.yml up -d --build` before looking for a code defect. Second hypothesis: the dispatch genuinely used one round (depth 3 triggers a continuation, which then compiles an empty plan and renders nothing, by design).
bugs.fix: NOT FIXED — user asked to note only. Next step: rebuild the cluster, then read node-a logs for 'compiling a continuation round'.

bugs.error_message: OPEN — reflect quotes a PREVIOUS turn's tool value: two dispatches minutes apart returned the same reversed string for different timestamps
bugs.root_cause: UNVERIFIED. Observed: dispatch 1 time=2026-09-12T18:30:52.901772712Z reply reversed=Z217277109.25:03:81T21-90-6202 (CORRECT). Dispatch 2 time=2026-09-12T18:36:19.391088723Z reply reversed=Z217277109.25:03:81T21-90-6202 (dispatch 1's value, wrong). reflect_only feeds the conversation tail (MAX_CONTEXT_TURNS) before the blackboard, so the composer appears to copy the earlier assistant message rather than the current results. Distinct from bug-212: the value is not invented, it is stale.
bugs.fix: NOT FIXED — user asked to note only. Candidate: make the current round's blackboard outrank conversation history in the reflect prompt, or test with the ${ref} substitution live (needs the cluster rebuilt).

bugs.error_message: Mojibake in every accented reply: 'chaÃ®ne inversÃ©e', 'caractÃ¨res'
bugs.root_cause: NOT the UI, as first assumed. `resolve_value` (planner/plan.rs) and `substitute_inline` (bindings/template.rs) both walked their input with a byte index and ended each iteration on `out.push(bytes[i] as char)`. That cast reads a single UTF-8 byte as a Latin-1 code point, so every multi-byte sequence came out as one mojibake character per byte: `î` (C3 AE) -> `Ã` + `®`. `resolve_value` runs over EVERY composer reply, so every accented assistant message was mangled. Located by elimination on the live cluster: the stored user turn was clean, the stored assistant turn was corrupt, Ollama queried directly answered cleanly, and a byte-inspecting proxy on the wire showed the LLM returning clean UTF-8 — so the corruption was inside n3ur0n, after serde_json::from_slice.
bugs.fix: Both loops now take the next `char` and advance by `len_utf8()`. Regression tests in each file; with the fix reverted they fail with left: 'La chaÃ®ne inversÃ©e est ruojnob â\u{80}\u{94} 7 caractÃ¨res'. Verified on the cluster: the same prompt now returns 'La chaîne "bonjour" inversée est "ruojnob" et elle contient 7 caractères', with no C3 83 byte anywhere in the response.

bugs.error_message: Uploading a file in the Files panel seems to do nothing
bugs.root_cause: Every upload is staged by store_local_cache, so a blob is always class D (Local cache). Starting an upload while Inbound or Outbound is selected put the file in a category the current view can never show: the grid stayed empty and the only clue was the 'n total' counter in the subtitle. Reproduced over CDP on a live node: server total 0 to 1, stored blob local_cache/outbound/input, view on class_b, 0 cards rendered.
bugs.fix: uploadFiles() reads the stored record back after refreshFiles(), computes blobClass() on it, and switches the sidebar category to where the file actually landed. The class is read off the record rather than hardcoded to D, so it still holds if the server ever classifies an upload differently. Regression-covered by scripts/ui-smoke.sh, which uploads from Inbound and asserts the category flips to class_d with one card.

bugs.error_message: The Files panel's Outbound section can never fill, and a sent file still shows as local cache
bugs.root_cause: record_outbound_upload wrote through blobs::upsert, whose ON CONFLICT(hash) updates size, mime, path, expiry, storage_path and status but deliberately never provenance/role/anchor_kind — that immutability is what stops a later write from relabelling an inbound result (B) or a cap staging blob (C). But the only blobs eligible for an outbound PUT are the ones already indexed as class D by store_local_cache, since prepare_invoke_args reads their bytes from the local store. So the D-to-A transition the spec describes (D is 'not yet referenced on the network') never happened: Outbound stayed empty forever and a file that had travelled still displayed 'local cache, staged'. Class A was only reachable for bytes sitting in blobs_dir with no index row, i.e. dropped on disk by hand.
bugs.fix: New storage::blobs::mark_outbound(hash, expires_at) issues an explicit UPDATE guarded by provenance='outbound' AND role='input' AND anchor_kind IN ('local_cache','user_session') — a clause that matches only classes A and D, so B (inbound/output) and C (cap_job) can never be caught. record_outbound_upload now promotes an existing row through it and only falls back to a fresh insert when no row exists. Covered by crates/node/tests/blob_outbound_promotion.rs against a wiremock peer, verified to fail without the fix (left: local_cache, right: user_session), plus three storage unit tests.

bugs.error_message: An uploaded blob vanishes from the publisher a few minutes after the transfer
bugs.root_cause: effective_expires() returned the ticket's expires_at whenever it was in the future, and a put ticket is authorized for TICKET_TTL_SECS = 300 s. So every blob stored through PUT /n3ur0n/v0/blobs got a five-minute lifetime instead of the one hour spec 5.1 prescribes, and the ten-minute GC sweep erased it. The fallback branch (now + default_ttl_secs) was unreachable: it only fired on an already-expired ticket, which verify_ticket rejects first. No symptom at upload time — 201 returned, the invoke ran, the store was empty minutes later. Found because node-b's cap-jobs listing and its blobs/sha256 directory were both empty right after a successful cluster transfer.
bugs.fix: effective_expires() now derives retention from ticket.purpose via default_ttl_secs, with requested_ttl_secs honoured up to a 7-day cap (spec 5.1) and clamped to the default below it. Two unit tests pin the distinction between the authorization window and the retention. Verified on the cluster: blobs now persist with expires_at at upload + 1 h, visible in /api/v0/cap-jobs/blobs and on disk.

bugs.error_message: The assistant answers the same message twice in one bubble: 'Hi to you!\n\nHi to you!'
bugs.root_cause: reflect_only built its prompt as system + state.to_chat_messages(MAX_CONTEXT_TURNS) + [re-stated user message]. dispatch_inner records the user turn BEFORE compiling, so the tail already contains it; the re-statement (added so the question sits after the blackboard and the tool turns) therefore appended a second identical user message. The model reads two consecutive identical user turns as two requests and answers both. Proven by logging the real prompt through an HTTP proxy in front of Ollama, then A/B against qwen2.5:7b with the same system prompt and tail, 3 runs each: one copy -> 'I tried to say hi to @peer:consumer#ivyrzhjr but encountered an issue'; two copies -> 'I tried to say hi ... TWICE, but the tool failed BOTH TIMES'. DirectChatPlanner was never affected: it relies on the tail alone.
bugs.fix: reflect_only drops the last role=='user' message from the tail before extending (tool results carry role 'tool', so the last user message is always the turn being answered), then re-states it once at the end. Regression test crates/node/tests/reflect_prompt.rs asserts the reflect prompt's user messages with a recording Backend, no LLM required; it fails without the fix with left: ['Hi to you!', 'Hi to you!']. Verified live through the proxy: reflect now carries one user message, both with an empty plan and with a tool step.

bugs.error_message: Direct chat mode still renders the plan-progress stepper: an empty box reading 'composing reply…' then 'done · <model>'
bugs.root_cause: appendStepper() already branched on isDirect for its initial status, but reflecting() did not: DirectChatPlanner emits PlanReady + Reflecting for stream symmetry, and the Reflecting branch overwrote the mode's line with the plan wording. finalize() then left the widget in place as 'done · model', duplicating the assistant bubble header, with no chips to inspect because direct mode compiles no plan. Every one of those status strings was also a hard-coded English literal in an otherwise translated panel. Observed in the browser over CDP: {cls:'stepper direct-mode no-plan', status:'composing reply…'} then {cls:'... complete', status:'done · qwen2.5:7b'}.
bugs.fix: reflecting() keeps composer.direct.status in direct mode; finalize() removes the widget entirely in direct mode (it survives on error, the one thing it still reports). Separately, every stepper status moved to i18n keys stepper.* in both locales. Verified over CDP on a live node: direct mode shows 'direct · rédaction de la réponse…' then zero .stepper elements; auto mode still shows 'compilation du plan…' → chip → 'terminé · qwen2.5:7b'. ui-smoke: 26 steps, no console errors.

bugs.error_message: A manifest-mode node cannot execute its own capability through the planner: `time` returns {} and the model reports it could not read the clock
bugs.root_cause: The plan executor dispatched any step with no endpoint through `node.backend()` — the single compile-time backend slot. In manifest mode that slot is deliberately filled with an inert EchoBackend (bootstrap.rs) because capabilities are supposed to dispatch through their own binding, which is exactly what handler.rs::invoke does for an inbound invoke. So a LOCAL step got Echo's identity of its arguments as its result: `time` with args {} answered {}, `random_int` answered {min,max} with no value. Remote steps were unaffected (they go over the wire and reach the peer's handler), which is why the same capability answered correctly to a signed invoke and wrongly to the node's own planner. Latent until node-a became the first manifest-mode node that both publishes caps and runs a planner.
bugs.fix: The local branch now mirrors handler.rs: registry.binding_for(cap) first, node.backend() only as the legacy fallback. Regression test crates/node/tests/local_step_uses_its_binding.rs builds a manifest-shaped node (inert Echo + a binding answering something the args do not contain) and executes a one-step plan; it fails without the fix with left: None. Verified on the cluster: time, random_int, reverse and string_length all return real values through the planner.

bugs.error_message: Cannot access '_activitySource' before initialization — the whole rail stops switching sections
bugs.root_cause: The activity block was appended at the end of app.js, including `let _activitySource = null;`. `activateSection` sits far above and calls `stopActivityStream()` for any section other than activity, and the bottom of the file runs `activateSection('chats')` at load. A `let` is hoisted but left uninitialised until its declaration executes, so that call threw in the temporal dead zone — and it threw from INSIDE activateSection, before the if/else chain, so every later rail click also died there: clicking Files while on Activity left the main pane showing Activity with the Files sidebar. The dashboard rendered nothing because the stream was never started either.
bugs.fix: The declaration moved next to `activateSection`, above its first use; the functions themselves stay at the bottom (function declarations hoist). Verified over CDP on node-b: zero console errors, tiles and rankings render, and clicking Files now hides the activity page and shows the files page.
